_comment: Speaker models (AI-8, spike S7, Oct 27 2026; since the maintainer decision of Oct 27 2026 both files SHIP INSIDE THE APP in Contents/Resources/Models/speaker, packaging/sherpa/fetch-models.sh, and these rows are the pins the bundled files are checked against; the url / import_only fields only serve a developer build without them and the CLI/MCP import): the two ONNX files the sherpa-onnx speaker engine needs. Same catalogue rules as models.json (sha256 and bytes are the pins; the store checks them after a download and on an import). pyannote segmentation-3.0 (converted by the sherpa-onnx project, MIT, Copyright (c) 2022 CNRS) and the 3D-Speaker CAM++ English VoxCeleb embedding model (Apache-2.0, from the 3D-Speaker repository and ModelScope record; the download comes without a licence file). Hashes and sizes were computed on the files downloaded for the spike (docs/project/spikes.md, S7). The segmentation model is published only inside a .tar.bz2 archive and the app does not unpack archives, so its row is import_only: the maintainer either hosts the extracted model.onnx at a fixed URL (then put it in url and remove import_only) or users import the file; the pins below are those of model.onnx inside the archive. To use another mirror put a catalog.json in the models folder: speaker rows are kept unless it names speaker models itself.

models.label: Speaker segmentation (pyannote 3.0)
models.hint: Finds where speech happens and who overlaps. First of the two files that tell speakers apart.
models.source: model.onnx inside https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases/download/speaker-segmentation-models/sherpa-onnx-pyannote-segmentation-3-0.tar.bz2 (6,958,444 bytes, SHA-256 24615ee884c897d9d2ba09bb4d30da6bb1b15e685065962db5b02e76e4996488): unpack the archive and import model.onnx

models.label: Speaker voices (CAM++ English)
models.hint: Compares voices so the same person gets the same label. Second of the two files that tell speakers apart.
